title: Harry and Meghan 'Surprised' by King's Letter About Their Royal Role
summary:
Imagine you move back to your old neighborhood, and then your grandpa sends a letter to everyone saying you're not allowed to help with the family business. That's kind of what happened to Prince Harry and Meghan!

Harry and Meghan used to be working royals—they did official events for the Queen and King. But in 2020, they decided to step back and live in California. Now they've moved back to the UK with their kids, Archie and Lilibet. But King Charles sent a letter to his representatives saying that Harry and Meghan are still not working royals. That means they can't do official royal events or represent the royal family.

Harry and Meghan's spokesperson said they were "a little surprised not to have been told about this in advance." They only saw the letter about an hour before it was shared with the media! That's like finding out about a big test the same day.

But royal sources say they were told before it went public. The letter also says that any charity work they do is personal, not royal. This is important because there's a meeting this week to decide how much security (police protection) they should get. Harry has complained before about not having enough protection in the UK.

So, what does this mean? Harry and Meghan can still do their own charity stuff, like the Invictus Games for injured soldiers. But they won't be representing the royal family. It's like being part of a club but not being on the team. They're back in the UK, but they're on their own.
why_it_matters: Even in a famous family, stepping away from a role can cause disagreements about rules, belonging, and what you are still allowed to do.

background_read: Prince Harry (King Charles's younger son) and Meghan (Harry's wife) used to be working royals who did official events for the royal family.
In 2020 they stepped back and moved to California, but now they have returned to the UK (the United Kingdom, where the king lives) with their children Archie and Lilibet.
King Charles (the British king) has sent a letter making clear that they are still not working royals and cannot do official royal duties.
Article_Structure: WHO: Prince Harry, Meghan, their children Archie and Lilibet, and King Charles's representatives and spokespeople.
WHAT: King Charles's letter says Harry and Meghan are still not working royals, and their spokesperson says they were not told about it in advance.
WHERE: In the UK, where Harry and Meghan have moved back with their children.
WHY: This is a family and palace dispute about official roles and security, and a meeting this week will decide how much protection they should get.

perspectives.description: They were surprised not to be told about the letter in advance and still want to do their own charity work instead of royal duties.
They believe the rules must be clear: if you leave your official royal role, you cannot keep acting as a working royal.
They are split between feeling sorry for Harry and Meghan and thinking the king is right to set boundaries about who represents the royal family.
